neighbours.label: The emotional effect on a person in conflict talk: 'how X made me feel', the hurt or harm caused, vs 'feel'/'how' in physical or procedural senses
fire: During the session she told her sister how the comment had made her feel.
Kids in the circle took turns saying how the teasing made them feel.
Instead of blaming him, explain how his silence makes you feel.
The counselor asked the boy to name the hurt his friend had caused.
In the letter he wrote about how the betrayal made him feel.
Good apologies acknowledge how your words made the other person feel.
The couple practiced saying how each argument left them feeling.
The victim was finally able to describe the hurt she had suffered.
quiet: During the session she told her sister how the oven had been fixed.
Kids in the circle took turns saying how the game should be scored.
Instead of guessing, explain how the new printer makes copies.
The doctor asked the boy to point to the bone he had broken.
In the letter he wrote about how the harvest went this year.
Good manuals explain how the parts fit together during assembly.
The couple practiced saying the names of the streets in French.
The mechanic was finally able to describe the noise the engine made.

predictions: 'made me feel' and hurt-caused items 0.3-1.1; tactile 'feel', mechanical 'how' under 0.1.
notes: Card: feelings, how (I am feeling), made him feel, impact, harm, grievances. Probe: 'made us feel' 1.146, 'describe the hurt' 0.425, 'repair the harm' 0.121, 'express your feelings' 0.133 (weak); 'feel of the leather' 0.010, 'explained how the pump' 0.006.
